title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 134
paragraphs: This Mys is known to have come to Lebadeia and to have persuaded one of the locals, by a payment of money, to descend to Trophonios; and he also came to the oracle at Abai of the Phokians. Moreover, when he came to Thebes for the first time, he not only consulted the Ismenian Apollo (where consultation is by victims, as at Olympia), but also, by payment, persuaded a stranger who was not a Theban and induced him to sleep in the temple of Amphiaraos. In this temple no Theban is permitted to seek divination, for the following reason: Amphiaraos, speaking through oracles, bade them choose which of two things they wanted — either to have him as a diviner, or as an ally in war — and refrain from the other use. They chose that he should be their ally in war; and for this reason no Theban is permitted to sleep in that temple.
